title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Model Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization & Regression Playbook
author: Priya Raman
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied ML evaluation practices into a single operational reference. It covers the eval harness onboarding process, prompt set and benchmark design, model onboarding criteria, quality guardrails, quantization profile integration, and regression triage procedures. The intended audience is ML engineers, model owners, and SREs responsible for model lifecycle and production quality.

Goals
- Ensure consistent, automated evaluations for every model variant before and after deployment.
- Maintain prompt sets and benchmarks that reflect production signal and customer-critical behaviors.
- Define clear triage and rollback procedures for regressions tied to quantization and model changes.
- Reduce time-to-resolution for quality incidents and prevent repeated flakiness.

Owners and Contacts
- Primary owner: Applied ML Platform (eng team)
- On-call triage lead: rotation (see team roster)
- Slack channel: #applied-ml-evals
- Pager: on-call SRE (see oncall schedule)

Key Definitions
- Eval harness: The CI/CD-integrated runner that executes prompt sets, collects metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, embedding-similarity, classification F1, hallucination rate), and records artifacts.
- Prompt set: A curated collection of prompts grouped by intent and priority (critical, high, medium).
- Regression: Any statistically significant degradation in defined metrics vs. a baseline model or approved threshold.
- Quantization profile: A set of knobs (bitwidths, per-channel vs per-tensor, calibration dataset) used to produce a quantized variant.

High-level Process (onboarding -> release -> monitoring)
1. Model candidate submission
   - Model owner opens a Model-Onboarding ticket and attaches model metadata: architecture, training data summary, size, expected latency, compatible runtimes (e.g., rv1-runtime, nvfuser), and initial quantization profile suggestions.
   - Template: `model-onboarding-template.md` (link in related pages).

2. Local eval harness smoke tests (developer)
   - Run the harness locally: `./eval-harness run --model ./model.pt --prompts prompts/critical.json --out artifacts/local-smoke`
   - Required: pass the smoke test (no crash, <5% timeout errors, sample outputs within expected token length).

3. CI / Pre-merge checks
   - The CI harness executes: unit tests, small-batch prompt sets, and quantization simulation.
   - Gates: latency budget (p50 < 150ms on reference hardware), memory < 90% of device, no new failing prompts in critical set.

4. Staging release + evaluation
   - Deploy model variant to staging cluster (dedicated lane) and run full prompt sets and workload replay for 24-72 hours.
   - Collect telemetry: token-level latency, per-prompt quality scores, top-k logits distribution, and hallucination annotations.

5. Canary and production rollout
   - Canary policy: 5% traffic for 24 hours, evaluate automatic regressions. If no regressions, progress to 25% then 100% by automated rollout policy.

Prompt Sets and Benchmarking
- Naming and structure: Use `intent.priority.vN.json` (e.g., `summarization.critical.v3.json`). Each prompt entry must include: id, prompt_text, expected_behavior, tags, and optional canonical_answer(s).
- Priority tiers:
  - Critical: customer-facing flows or safety-sensitive prompts. Zero regressions accepted; threshold lambda = 0.
  - High: high-frequency product flows. Allow minor variance but monitor drift (>2% change triggers triage).
  - Medium: exploratory or low-frequency cases. Use for capacity planning and non-blocking alerts.

Example prompt JSON schema (snippet)
{
  "id": "summ-crit-001",
  "prompt": "Summarize the following support ticket in two sentences: ...",
  "expected": "Concise summary capturing issue and requested action",
  "tags": ["summarization","support"]
}

Benchmarks and Metrics
- Core metrics recorded per prompt: accuracy/F1 (if label exists), ROUGE-L, embedding-similarity (cosine to golden answer), hallucination-rate (annotated), latency p50/p95/p99, token-efficiency (tokens generated / useful_tokens).
- Acceptance criteria for release: critical set must not regress by >0.5% absolute on embedding-similarity and must maintain latency SLOs (p95 < configured by target runtime).

Quality Guardrails
- Automated checks integrated into harness:
  - Toxicity filter: automatic reject if toxic-score > 0.7 (model-specific threshold).
  - Hallucination detector: flag responses that claim unsupported facts (heuristic + classifier).
  - Output length sanity: enforce max tokens per intent.
- Manual review: any flagged critical prompt enters manual QA with the model owner and applied ML lead.

Quantization Profiles and Integration
- Profile naming: `profile.{bitwidth}.{per-channel|per-tensor}.{calib-dataset}` e.g., `profile.4.per-channel.docs-cord-2026`.
- Integration steps:
  1. Generate quantized variant using quant tool: `quantize --model model.pt --profile profile.4.per-channel --out model.q4.pt`
  2. Run quantization regression suite (subset of prompt sets tuned for quant-specific failure modes).
  3. Compare distribution shift: KL-divergence of logits, embedding-similarity drop, and per-prompt quality delta.
- Acceptance: quantized variant accepted if critical set change <= 1.0% embedding-similarity absolute and latency improvement >= 20% on target hardware. If either fails, iterate on profile or fall back to a less aggressive profile.

Regression Detection & Triage Playbook
- Detection sources: CI pre-merge, staging automated jobs, production monitors (daily batch eval on sampled production traces).
- Automatic alerting thresholds:
  - Critical metric regression: any absolute drop > 0.5% triggers a P1 alert.
  - High-priority drift: 0.5%-2% drop -> P2 review.
  - Latency SLO breach: p95 > SLO for > 10 minutes -> P1.

Immediate Triage Steps (P1)
1. Acknowledge alert and assign incident lead (model owner or on-call applied-ml engineer).
2. Reproduce: run the eval harness against the failing baseline and current candidate over the same seed and prompt subset. Command: `./eval-harness compare --baseline s3://models/baseline --candidate s3://models/candidate --prompts critical-set.json --out /tmp/reg-compare`
3. Collect artifacts: raw outputs, per-prompt metrics, sampling traces, and runtime telemetry.
4. Preliminary classification (1-3):
   - Classification 1: infrastructure/regression (GPU kernel issue, runtime change).
   - Classification 2: model-quality regression (training data drift, objective change, quantization artifact).
   - Classification 3: prompt/benchmark drift (broken canonical answers or changed production signal).
5. Remediation path by classification:
   - Infra: engage eng-serving-runtime, rollback runtime change or pin kernel.
   - Model-quality: rollback model, open model fix PR, expand training or re-calibrate quantization.
   - Prompt drift: update prompt set or labels; if critical, escalate to product and customer success.
6. Postmortem within 3 business days for P1 incidents; include root cause, fix, and preventive actions.

Rollback and Canary Safety Controls
- Canary auto-rollback: configured when critical metric drops > 0.5% or latency increase > 25% during canary window.
- Manual abort: product or security can abort rollout at any stage.

Example Runbook: Reproducing a Quantization Regression
1. Checkout model tag and quant profile: `git checkout tags/model-v2 && git checkout quant-profiles/profile.4.per-channel`
2. Recreate quant artifact: `quantize --model ./model-v2.pt --profile profile.4.per-channel --out ./model-v2.q4.pt`
3. Run harness compare: `./eval-harness compare --baseline ./model-v2.pt --candidate ./model-v2.q4.pt --prompts ./prompts/critical.json --metrics embedding-similarity,rouge,latency --out ./artifacts/quant-reg`
4. Inspect `artifacts/quant-reg/summary.csv` and `artifacts/quant-reg/failed_prompts.json` for top offenders.

Metrics Export and Dashboards
- Export job (daily): run batch eval across a rolling window of production prompts (sample size configurable; default 10k prompts/day) and push metrics to MetricsDB under `applied_ml.evals.daily`.
- Dashboards:
  - Eval Health (per-model): embedding-similarity, hallucination-rate, latency p50/p95/p99, prompt-failure heatmap.
  - Quantization Impact: per-profile summary of metric deltas and cost savings.

Governance and Review cadence
- Quarterly model reviews: owners present model performance vs. product KPIs and call out planned quantization/architecture changes.
- Prompt set housekeeping: owners to review critical and high prompt sets monthly and archive deprecated prompts.

Appendix: Templates and Useful Commands
- Model onboarding checklist (short):
  1. Completed model metadata + training data summary.
  2. Local smoke tests passed.
  3. CI pre-merge eval green.
  4. Staging 24-72h perf and quality pass.
  5. Canary with no critical regressions.

- Useful CLI snippets:
`# Run full regression suite`
`./eval-harness run --model s3://models/candidate --prompts s3://prompts/full-bench.json --out s3://artifacts/candidate-reg`

`# Generate quant artifact`
`quantize --model s3://models/candidate --profile profile.4.per-channel.docs-cord-2026 --out s3://models/candidate-q4`

- Example artifact table (CSV columns recommended):
| model_tag | profile | metric | baseline_score | candidate_score | delta | pass_fail | notes |
|----------|---------|--------|----------------|-----------------|-------|-----------|-------|
| model-v2 | q4pc   | embed_sim | 0.912 | 0.901 | -0.011 | FAIL | large drop on legal-summ prompts |
